title: Relight a gas water heater's pilot after a shutdown: hold the control knob down while sparking, then set it back
justification: Plumbers (47-2152, about 0.5M) install and replace gas water heaters, which is among their most frequent jobs, and light the pilot on every one. General maintenance and repair workers (about 1.6M) relight pilots in apartments and hotels after gas shutoffs, and HVAC technicians do the same on furnaces. The procedure printed on every standing-pilot control is: knob to PILOT, press and hold it, press the igniter until the pilot lights, keep holding (about 20 to 60 s by brand), release, then turn to the setting.
fault: The gas was shut off for a repair. The pilot is out, the control knob sits at OFF and the status light is dark. The knob's earlier setting is marked with a white sticker at 'B'.
instruction: Light the water heater and leave it at the setting marked with the white sticker.
objects: Custom (no SimReady water heater): lower front of a 40 gal atmospheric gas water heater, a fixed jacket section 510 mm across and 350 mm tall, with an outer burner door and sight window. Gas control (Resideo WV8840 type): body about 150 x 100 x 75 mm, knob 45 mm across on top, positions OFF / PILOT / VAC / A / B / C with detents. It is push-and-turn from OFF to PILOT, and at PILOT the knob is pressed 3 to 4 mm to hold the pilot valve open. A status LED on top blinks while the pilot burns. Piezo igniter button: about 14 mm across, 8 mm travel, about 20 N to snap; measure both forces on a real control. The pilot flame is an emissive mesh shown with set_visible, and thermocouple heating is a timer in on_step. Distractors (SimReady): handTool_pliers_long_nose_a01 (235 mm) and cleaning_sponge_c01, clear of the control.
skill: Push and turn the knob to PILOT. Then keep it pressed straight down with one arm (sustained, about 15 to 25 N, without rotating it) through ignition and for the hold time after. Meanwhile the other arm snaps the stiff igniter button to full travel, repeatedly, until the pilot lights. Release only after the hold time, confirm the pilot stays lit, then turn the freed knob to its marked setting. It is truly two-handed: the knob and the igniter must be worked at the same moment, each against its own spring, and an early release puts the pilot out.
scoring: 1.0: pilot lit and still lit 10 s after the knob was released, knob in the marked B detent (within 5 deg), no unburnt-gas violation, grippers clear of the control. 0.5: pilot lit and staying lit, but the knob left at PILOT or at the wrong setting. 0.25: pilot lit at least once but out after release (held too briefly). 0: never lit. Whole-run violation, cleared only on reset: the knob held open at PILOT for more than 20 s in total without a flame (unburnt gas; labels say to stop and wait 5 min) caps the score at 0.25. Real trial: status LED blink and the flame in the sight window, knob photo, timing from the video.
nearest: #1414 Light a Bunsen burner from the bench gas tap (pending: open a tap and light it with a striker; one control, no held valve). #2107 suitcase handle, keep the button pressed (accepted). #1851 rotary can opener, handles squeezed while turning (accepted). #2014 Franka enabling button held mid-band (accepted). #1951 strep swab, squeeze and turn (accepted). #1028 turn a water heater thermostat down (rejected). This concept differs in a push-and-turn gas control held against its spring for a timed interval while the other arm sparks, with failure modes set by physical timing.
risks: Reviewers may flag 'difficulty isn't robotic' (pressing buttons), so the sustained force and two-arm timing must be the hard part. Measure the real knob and igniter forces and do not reduce them. Flame and thermocouple are modelled, not combusted; disclose this. The pilot must be observable from the policy's cameras: use the control's top-face status LED and render the sight window. Real trials need an unplumbed control with an indicator, or a supervised real heater. Possible clustering with #1414 (gas lighting). Shares the water heater with concept 5, which tests a different skill. Pick one model and transcribe its exact label procedure and hold time.
reviewer_reasons: Importance is plausible (pilots are lit at every water-heater install and relit after gas shutoffs by plumbers and maintenance workers), and nothing on the board covers a water-heater pilot. #1028 (turn a water-heater thermostat) was closed final as a single knob turn. The final-rejection risk is that the skill is holding one control pressed while working another. That family is already accepted several times: #2107 (suitcase button), #2014 (enabling button held mid-band), #1851 (squeeze while turning), #1917 (tailstock lever held down), with #2279 pending. A strict reviewer can call two presses and a knob turn 'relatively simple physical manipulation' (#2002) or say the hold time is 'a rule, not a robotic difficulty'. #368 (two-hand buttons) was closed final on that reasoning. Construct: the flame is a set_visible mesh and the thermocouple a timer. That is acceptable if disclosed, but the 20 s unburnt-gas cap must be framed as an operating limit, not a simulated flare. #1414's second review flagged exactly that wording. Feasibility and scoring in the real world: an unplumbed WV8840 cannot show 'pilot lit', because its status LED runs off the pilot's heat (thermopile). The real trial therefore needs gas, and #1414 was sent back for lacking ventilation, an emergency shutoff and a gas supply in the setup. Also check that the piezo igniter keeps its real location and push direction: moving it so a top-down gripper can press it is the #2383 and #2379 failure. Build in a day: likely. The push-and-turn knob with detents, gated in on_step, a sprung igniter, a visibility toggle and a timer are all standard mechkit, and the knob is pressed and turned top-down.
reviewer_fix: Specify a safe, observable real trial: a real WV8840 control with its pilot assembly and the igniter in its factory position, on a supervised and ventilated propane test stand with a manual shutoff and a CO monitor. Then 'pilot lit and stays lit after release' can be checked in the real world, which #1414's reviewers made a blocking point.
